patent.title: Organic electroluminescent devices having improved power conversion efficiencies
patent.family_note: Improved-efficiency thin-film organic EL follow-on to Tang US4356429A (organic electroluminescent cell, granted 1982-10-26). Package B early ledger uses APL publication-date T0=1987-09-21 (post-grant, pre-commercial); later commercial OLED products are excluded from this historical state.

knowledge_origin.description: Public patent record identifies Eastman Kodak industrial R&D inventorship (Tang / VanSlyke) and corporate ownership of the improved thin-film organic EL device.

technology.problem: Prior organic EL cells (including thick-film / high-voltage and earlier thin-film constructions) lacked power conversion efficiency at low driving voltages needed for economical drive circuitry and practical thin-film devices.
technology.mechanism: Bilayer / zoned thin-film organic electroluminescent device with a hole-injecting zone and an organic luminescent zone, enabling improved power conversion efficiency at low voltage in a ≤~1 µm active stack.
technology.comparison_baseline: Earlier organic EL approaches requiring high drive voltage and/or showing lower power conversion efficiency at ≤25 V (including the Kodak / Tang 1982 porphyrinic hole-injecting cell as an improved but still insufficient baseline called out in the patent).

value_carriers.name: Low-voltage organic EL / OLED display-emissive platform (aspirational at T0; no marketed carrier confirmed)
value_carriers.description: Pre-T0 Kodak patents and the 1987 APL paper demonstrate lab-device brightness/efficiency at low voltage, but at T0=1987-09-21 no public exact-patent mapping to a marketed OLED display product is used in this ledger.

gaps.description: At T0=1987-09-21 there is no confirmed exact-patent → marketed OLED display / product carrier link in this ledger. Lab-device performance and claimed EL device uses are not implemented as a public commercial carrier here.
needed_evidence: license / supply schedule tying this grant to a marketed display

gaps.description: No public T0 evidence attributes royalty, incremental display revenue, or cost/performance economics to this exact patent.
V0.7 can record R0 plus scientific / device differentiation, but has no structured field for early option/future-value horizon that is decision-relevant precisely when realization is still R0/R1.
needed_evidence: explicit separation of option signals from realized R-stage

notes: Package B early-stage option retrospective #2 (non-life-science). T0=APL publication 1987-09-21 stops at R0: Kodak industrial patent + prior 1982 platform patent + peer-reviewed bright low-voltage organic EL diode signal exist, but no marketed exact-patent carrier is recorded. Pioneer GD-F1 (1997), later phone/TV OLED products, and licensing narratives are post-T0 and must not be backfilled into this ledger.
